primary_task: Build an MCP server (TypeScript MCP SDK or Python FastMCP) that wraps an external service's API, verify it compiles, and test it with the MCP Inspector.

requirements.name: node/npm (TypeScript) or python (Python)
requirements.evidence: Run `npm run build` to verify compilation ... Verify syntax: `python -m py_compile your_server.py` (alternatives: TypeScript or Python)
requirements.basis: "bash": "run shell commands on Linux x86_64: install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, npm, apt from Ubuntu, go modules, nuget, GitHub release downloads), build, test, run CLIs and scripts ..."

requirements.name: MCP SDK (@modelcontextprotocol/sdk or mcp/FastMCP) and zod/pydantic
requirements.evidence: whether in Python (FastMCP) or Node/TypeScript (MCP SDK) ... Use Zod (TypeScript) or Pydantic (Python)

requirements.name: modelcontextprotocol.io
requirements.evidence: Start with the sitemap to find relevant pages: `https://modelcontextprotocol.io/sitemap.xml`
requirements.basis: "network access to hosts outside the egress allow-list: only PyPI, npm, GitHub, Ubuntu apt archives, NuGet and the Go module proxy are open; other hosts are refused" (modelcontextprotocol.io is in neither egress_allow nor egress_deny; _sources: "hosts not listed are unknown")

requirements.name: target external service API credentials
requirements.evidence: API client with authentication ... Content Exploration: Use READ-ONLY operations to explore available data
requirements.basis: "accounts, logins, API keys or credentials for external services other than the listed connectors and GitHub" (lacks) — depends on which service is wrapped; available only if it is GitHub, unavailable for other SaaS

requirements.name: web_fetch / web_search
requirements.evidence: Review the service's API documentation ... Use web search and WebFetch as needed.
requirements.basis: "web_fetch": "fetch a web page or unauthenticated API by URL; hosts outside the egress allow-list are refused"; "web_search": "search the public web and read result snippets"

notes: Reading taken: the core deliverable is the MCP server code that builds and starts under the Inspector; documentation fetching and Phase 4 evaluations (which need live data from the wrapped service) are supporting/follow-up. Unknown: modelcontextprotocol.io reachability (check with a fetch). Other reading: if the Phase 4 evaluations against real service data are counted as part of the deliverable and the wrapped service is a non-GitHub SaaS, credential:service-api would be hard and unavailable, giving BLOCKED; for a GitHub-wrapping server it stays ACHIEVABLE.
